categories.summary: Saudi air defences destroyed a Houthi cruise missile over Riyadh on 28 November with no damage (confirmed by the Saudi-led coalition). We found no newly confirmed attacks on US bases, tankers or Gulf oil sites since then. Iranian state media report blasts in Riyadh and Iran claims more tankers hit mines in Hormuz; neither is independently confirmed. GPS jamming over the Persian Gulf has been high for about 12 hours, which is routine there. Taiwan and Korea are quiet.

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command aircraft are normal. Forecast markets give a Russian or US nuclear test this year only about 2%.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: Britain's pensions and benefits department (DWP) confirmed a cyber attack that took some services offline; payments are unaffected and the attacker is not known. Hong Kong's Octopus payment card reports a data breach. These add to a run of big hacks this week (Flight Centre, the European Commission, US intelligence systems, Switzerland). The suspected China campaign, partly blamed on China by governments, touches Australia. Australian phones, banks and the grid look normal, but our phone-network and internet monitors are timing out.

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports bird flu (H5N1) in the United States, Ebola in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, and MERS in Qatar; none is spreading toward Australia. No Adelaide emergency departments are flagged as very busy.

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is Moderate today and tomorrow; Adelaide has no rating. No fire bans, CFS warnings or Watch and Act messages, and no CFS incidents near home. Sunday is cool (about 17°C) with gusts near 55 km/h. Some outback roads remain closed by flooding. A magnitude 6.7 earthquake hit Kamchatka in far-east Russia, a long way from Australia.

categories.summary: Gold rose about 3.7%, a sign of nervous investors, while the US 'fear gauge' (VIX) eased to about 24 and oil fell. The Australian dollar is about 66.5 US cents. No sign of bank trouble in Australia.

drivers: A run of big hacks continues: Britain's pensions and benefits department confirmed a cyber attack this week, after Flight Centre in Australia, the European Commission and US intelligence systems. Who is behind the DWP attack is not known.

If the China-linked hacking is one deliberate campaign, the likely aim is quiet footholds in allies' phone, power and water networks ahead of any Taiwan crisis, with phone networks, utilities and ports the likely next targets. This is a hypothesis, though governments have blamed China for parts of it.
Suspected Iran-linked attacks on shop freezers and small water systems remain overseas.

headline: No new confirmed attacks on US bases, tankers or Gulf oil sites since Saturday's Riyadh missile was shot down; SA fuel is steady and Hills fire danger is only Moderate today and tomorrow.
summary: We checked for new attacks on US bases, tankers and Gulf cities and oil sites in the last day and found no newly confirmed hits; Iran and Iranian media again claim tanker hits and blasts in Riyadh, which are not confirmed. Oil is near US$91 and SA fuel is steady. Britain's pensions and benefits department confirmed a cyber attack (payments unaffected), the latest in a run of big overseas hacks. Fire danger near home is Moderate today and tomorrow with no warnings; Sunday is cool and still windy.
